sentences: Two years ago, Rupert Murdoch's daughter, Elisabeth, spoke of the "unsettling dearth of integrity across so many of our institutions".
Integrity had collapsed, she argued, because of a collective acceptance that the only "sorting mechanism" in society should be profit and the market.
But "it's us, human beings, we the people who create the society we want, not profit."
translations: 两年前，鲁珀特·默多克的女儿伊丽莎白谈到了“我们众多机构中令人不安的诚信缺失”。
她认为，诚信之所以崩溃，是因为人们集体接受了一种观念，即社会中唯一的“筛选机制”应当是利润和市场。
但是，“是我们，是人类，是我们人民创造了我们想要的社会，而不是利润。”

sentences: Driving her point home, she continued: "It's increasingly apparent that the absence of purpose, of a moral language within government, media or business could become one of the most dangerous goals for capitalism and freedom."

This same absence of moral purpose was wounding companies such as News International, she thought, making it more likely that it would lose its way as it had with widespread illegal telephone hacking.
translations: 为了把她的观点讲透彻，她继续说道：“越来越明显的是，政府、媒体或商业内部缺乏目标、缺乏道德语言，可能成为资本主义和自由最危险的目标之一。”
她认为，同样缺乏道德目标正在伤害像新闻国际这样的公司，使其更有可能像在广泛的非法电话窃听事件中那样迷失方向。

sentences: As the hacking trial concludes – finding guilty one ex-editor of the News of the World, Andy Coulson, for conspiring to hack phones, and finding his predecessor, Rebekah Brooks, innocent of the same charge – the wider issue of dearth of integrity still stands.
Journalists are known to have hacked the phones of up to 5,500 people.
This is hacking on an industrial scale, as was acknowledged by Glenn Mulcaire, the man hired by the News of the World in 2001 to be the point person for phone hacking.
Others await trial.
This long story still unfolds.
translations: 随着窃听案审判的结束——判定《世界新闻报》前编辑安迪·库尔森因共谋窃听电话而有罪，并判定其前任丽贝卡·布鲁克斯在同样的指控上无罪——更广泛的诚信缺失问题依然存在。
据悉，记者们曾窃听过多达5500人的电话。
这是工业规模的窃听行为，正如格伦·穆尔凯尔所承认的那样，他于2001年被《世界新闻报》雇佣，担任电话窃听的关键人物。
其他人等待审判。
这个漫长的故事仍在展开。

sentences: In many respects, the dearth of moral purpose frames not only the fact of such widespread phone hacking but the terms on which the trial took place.
One of the astonishing revelations was how little Rebekah Brooks knew of what went on in her newsroom, how little she thought to ask and the fact that she never inquired how the stories arrived.
The core of her successful defence was that she knew nothing.
translations: 在许多方面，道德目标的缺失不仅构成了这种广泛电话窃听行为的事实背景，也构成了审判进行的条件。
令人震惊的揭露之一是，丽贝卡·布鲁克斯对她的新闻编辑室里发生的事情知之甚少，她很少想到去询问，而且她从未追问过这些报道是如何得来的。
她成功辩护的核心是她一无所知。

sentences: In today's world, it has become normal that well-paid executives should not be accountable for what happens in the organisations that they run.
Perhaps we should not be so surprised.
For a generation, the collective doctrine has been that the sorting mechanism of society should be profit.
The words that have mattered are efficiency, flexibility, shareholder value, business-friendly, wealth generation, sales, impact and, in newspapers, circulation.
Words degraded to the margin have been justice, fairness, tolerance, proportionality and accountability.
translations: 在当今世界，高薪高管不必为他们所经营的组织中发生的事情负责，这已成为常态。
也许我们不应该如此惊讶。
对于一代人来说，集体信条一直是社会的筛选机制应当是利润。
重要的词汇是效率、灵活性、股东价值、商业友好、财富创造、销售、影响力，以及在报纸行业中的发行量。
被边缘化的词汇是正义、公平、宽容、相称性和问责制。

sentences: The purpose of editing the News of the World was not to promote reader understanding, to be fair in what was written or to betray any common humanity.
It was to ruin lives in the quest for circulation and impact.
Ms Brooks may or may not have had suspicions about how her journalists got their stories, but she asked no questions, gave no instructions – nor received traceable, recorded answers.
translations: 编辑《世界新闻报》的目的不是为了促进读者的理解，不是为了对所写内容保持公正，也不是为了背叛任何共同的人性。
而是为了追求发行量和影响力而毁掉人们的生活。
布鲁克斯女士可能怀疑也可能不怀疑她的记者们是如何获得报道的，但她没有提出任何问题，没有给出任何指示——也没有收到可追踪的、有记录的答复。

sentences:
36. According to the first two paragraphs, Elisabeth was upset by____
A. the consequences of the current sorting mechanism.
B. companies' financial loss due to immoral practices.
C. governmental ineffectiveness on moral issues.
D. the wide misuse of integrity among institutions.
translations:
36. 根据前两段，伊丽莎白对____感到不安。
A. 当前分类机制带来的后果。
B. 公司因不道德行为而遭受的经济损失。
C. 政府在道德问题上的无效作为。
D. 诚信在机构中被广泛滥用。

sentences:
37. It can be inferred from Paragraph 3 that____
A. Glenn Mulcaire may deny phone hacking as a crime.
B. more journalists may be found guilty of phone hacking.
C. Andy Coulson should be held innocent of the charge.
D. phone hacking will be accepted on certain occasions.
translations:
37. 从第三段可以推断出____。
A. 格伦·穆尔凯尔可能否认电话窃听是犯罪。
B. 更多记者可能被判犯有电话窃听罪。
C. 安迪·库尔森应被认定无罪。
D. 电话窃听在某些情况下会被接受。

sentences:
38. The author believes that Rebekah Brooks's defence____
A. was hardly convincing.
B. centered on trivial issues.
C. revealed a cunning personality.
D. was part of a conspiracy.
translations:
38. 作者认为丽贝卡·布鲁克斯的辩护____。
A. 很难令人信服。
B. 集中在琐碎问题上。
C. 显示出狡猾的性格。
D. 是阴谋的一部分。

sentences:
39. The author holds that the current collective doctrine shows
A. a marginalized lifestyle.
B. unfair wealth distribution.
C. generally distorted values.
D. a rigid moral code.
translations:
39. 作者认为当前的集体信条显示出____。
A. 边缘化的生活方式。
B. 不公平的财富分配。
C. 普遍扭曲的价值观。
D. 僵化的道德准则。

sentences:
40. Which of the following is suggested in the last paragraph?
A. The quality of writings is of primary importance.
B. Moral awareness matters in editing a newspaper.
C. Common humanity is central to news reporting.
D. Journalists need stricter industrial regulations.
translations:
40. 最后一段暗示了以下哪一点？
A. 写作质量至关重要。
B. 道德意识在编辑报纸中很重要。
C. 共同的人性对新闻报道至关重要。
D. 记者需要更严格的行业规范。
